title: 8 Limbs of Yoga
tagline: Ashtanga — the complete path of yoga

sutra.sanskrit: Yama (moral injunctions), Niyama (observances), Āsana (posture), Prāṇāyāma (regulation of breath), Pratyāhāra (withholding of senses), Dhāraṇā (fixity of attention), Dhyāna (meditation), and Samādhi (absorption of consciousness in the self) are the eight accessories (limbs) of Yoga
sutra.meaning: Yoga is a complete lifestyle.

sutra.sanskrit: Once this is accomplished, regulation of the incoming and the outgoing breath with retention is attained.
sutra.meaning: Prana is the all permeating, auto generated  energy which sustains and destroys life. It is also at the heart of the practice of yoga.  Pranayama consists of prana + ayama ie regulation. Prana is vital to maintaining life and the systems of the body. Pranayama helps to keep its free flow.

sections.shlokaFrom: Still others offer as sacrifice the outgoing breath in the incoming breath, while some offer the incoming breath into the outgoing breath. Some arduously practice prāṇāyām and restrain the incoming and outgoing breaths, purely absorbed in the regulation of the life-energy. Yet others curtail their food intake and offer the breath into the life-energy as sacrifice. All these knowers of sacrifice are cleansed of their impurities as a result of such performances.

sutra.sanskrit: Pranayam has three movements : regulated inhalation, exhalation and retention as per the sadhak's capacity.
sutra.meaning: Pranayam need to be practiced with awareness as per ones capacity over a long period of time.Practice everday gradually increasing the capacity of the lungs.

sections.insight: Am I practicing pranayam with attention and ease?
sections.reflectionPrompt: practice alternate nostril breathing at a very slow rate, for 9 rotations, focusing on inhalation for 4 , retention 2  and exhalation 6 counts.

sutra.sanskrit: That which transcends the objective external and internal breath regulation is the fourth type of pranayama.
sutra.meaning: The fourth type of Pranayama goes beyond inhalation,exhalation amd retention. It happens of its own volition wherein a state of pause is experienced in both the breath and the mind. Therefore it is rightly called nirbeej pranayam. This is experienced by sadhak's doing a long session of pranayam for instance during Long kriya.

sutra.sanskrit: From that is dissipated, the mental darkness which veils the light, ... and from that, is attained the state of the mind for linking the attention to a higher concentration force or person.

sutra.meaning: Pranayama removes the veil covering the light of knowledge and heralds the dawn of wisdom.
